summary: Kosovo waives short-stay visas (stays under 3 months) for the EU and Schengen area, the US, UK and Canada, most of Latin America and the Caribbean, the Gulf states, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Israel, Turkey and much of the Pacific, and for its neighbors; holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa or Schengen residence permit can also visit for up to 15 days without a Kosovo visa. Other nationalities, including Bosnia and Herzegovina, apply at a Kosovo embassy.

conditionalWaivers.text: Nationals who otherwise need a visa can enter Kosovo without one, for up to 15 days, if they hold a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa or a valid biometric residence permit issued by a Schengen state. Kosovo's Ministry of Foreign Affairs names no such exemption for US or UK visas.

fee.notes: Application fee for a short-stay visa, set by Kosovo's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Holders of diplomatic and official passports are exempt. Pay by bank transfer to the account given by the Kosovo embassy or consulate where you apply.

source.name: Embassies of the Republic of Kosovo (MFA) — Visas for foreign nationals
source.instrument: Fee: Kosovo Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa page (EUR 40 for a C visa). Stay and decision period: Law No. 04/L-219 on Foreigners (https://gzk.rks-gov.net/ActDetail.aspx?ActID=8876), Article 23 (decision within 15 calendar days, extendable to 30, or to 60 where additional documents are required), and Article 38 as amended by Law No. 06/L-036, Article 6 (https://gzk.rks-gov.net/ActDetail.aspx?ActID=16333): a short stay is up to 90 days within 180 days.

fee.notes: For stays longer than 3 months, followed by a residence permit in Kosovo. Exempt: holders of diplomatic and official passports, children under 6, and pupils, students and accompanying teachers travelling for study or training. Pay by bank transfer to the account given by the Kosovo embassy or consulate where you apply.

source.name: Embassies of the Republic of Kosovo (MFA) — Visas for foreign nationals
source.instrument: Fee: Kosovo Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa page (EUR 80 for a D visa). Decision period: Law No. 04/L-219 on Foreigners (https://gzk.rks-gov.net/ActDetail.aspx?ActID=8876), Article 23 (decision within 15 calendar days, extendable to 30, or to 60 where additional documents are required).

passportValidity.text: Kosovo's Ministry of Foreign Affairs requires visa applicants to show a passport valid for at least 3 months beyond their planned departure from Kosovo, with at least two blank pages. It states no separate rule for visa-free visitors; the UK government says a British passport must be undamaged and valid for the length of the stay. Citizens of EU and Schengen states, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino, the Holy See, Albania, Montenegro and Serbia can enter with a valid biometric ID card.

source.name: Embassies of the Republic of Kosovo (MFA) — Visas for foreign nationals

travelInsurance.text: Visa applicants must show health insurance valid in Kosovo for the whole stay, according to Kosovo's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. No official source we could read states an insurance requirement for visa-free visitors. The UK government says Kosovo's public health system is poorly funded and advises adequate travel health insurance.

safety.text: The UK government's travel advice says the political situation is generally stable, but there is a risk of protests in the northern municipalities of Zvečan, Zubin Potok and Leposavić and in Mitrovica north of the Ibar, which have at times turned violent; Canada advises against non-essential travel to Leposavić, North Mitrovica, Zubin Potok and Zvečan. The UK government says pickpockets operate in airports and on public transport, and in September 2026 it reported large evening gatherings in Pristina and other urban centres, advising travellers to allow extra time and stay away from large crowds.

tips.text: The UK government says you cannot travel from Kosovo to Serbia without a Serbian entry stamp and are likely to be refused entry without one; Serbia does not treat its crossing points with Kosovo as international border crossings. It advises taking a route through a third country.

Canada advises against non-essential travel to northern Kosovo, and the UK government warns that protests in Zvečan, Zubin Potok, Leposavić and north Mitrovica have at times turned violent and advises avoiding large crowds and demonstrations.

If you hold a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa or a Schengen biometric residence permit, you can enter Kosovo without a Kosovo visa for a short visit of up to 15 days. US and UK visas are not on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' list.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Kosovo?
faq.answer: Probably not: Kosovo's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists the nationalities that need no short-stay visa (stays under 3 months), including EU and Schengen-area citizens, the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Israel, the Gulf states, most of Latin America and the Caribbean, many Pacific island states, and its neighbors Albania, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. Holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa or a Schengen biometric residence permit can also enter visa-free for up to 15 days. Other nationalities, including Bosnia and Herzegovina, apply at a Kosovo embassy.

faq.question: Can I enter Kosovo with a Schengen visa?
faq.answer: Yes — holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa, or of a biometric residence permit issued by a Schengen state, can enter Kosovo without a Kosovo visa for up to 15 days. Kosovo's Ministry of Foreign Affairs names no such exemption for US or UK visas, and a single-entry Schengen visa does not qualify.

faq.question: Can I travel between Kosovo and Serbia?
faq.answer: Crossings operate, but direction matters. The UK government says Serbia does not consider its crossing points with Kosovo to be official international border crossings: you can travel from Serbia to Kosovo and back, but not from Kosovo into Serbia without a Serbian entry stamp. It advises taking a route through a third country.

faq.question: What currency is used in Kosovo?
faq.answer: The euro. Canada's travel advice says Kosovo's economy is largely cash-based, with credit cards accepted in some larger establishments and cash machines in urban centres.

faq.question: Is Kosovo part of the Schengen Area or the EU?
faq.answer: No. The European Commission says the Schengen area is made up of 29 countries — 25 EU member states plus Iceland, Norway, Switzerland and Liechtenstein — and Kosovo is not among them.

faq.question: How are Kosovar passport holders treated abroad?
faq.answer: Regulation (EU) 2023/850 exempts holders of biometric passports issued by Kosovo from the visa requirement for travel to the EU Member States, from 1 January 2024 at the latest. No official source we could read covers how other countries treat the passport.
